sections.content: You know the imperfect (A2 Unit 21), the present perfect (A2 Unit 1) and, from this unit, reciprocal verbs, *soler* and relative clauses. When describing a difficult relationship, Spanish combines them. The new point is the contrast: the imperfect for what used to be the case, the present perfect for a change that matters now.

items.spanish: Aunque antes discutíamos mucho, últimamente nos hemos acercado porque hemos aprendido a escucharnos.
items.english: Although we used to argue a lot, lately we have become closer because we have learned to listen to each other.

items.spanish: La persona con quien tuve el desacuerdo ha cambiado, y ahora confiamos más el uno en el otro.
items.english: The person I had the disagreement with has changed, and now we trust each other more.

items.spanish: Nos reuníamos cada semana, pero nos distanciamos cuando dejamos de compartir nuestras preocupaciones.
items.english: We used to meet every week, but we grew apart when we stopped sharing our concerns.

items.spanish: Después del malentendido, nos reconciliamos y hemos recuperado una relación que ahora es más tranquila.
items.english: After the misunderstanding, we made up and have recovered a relationship that is now calmer.

sections.content: Interpersonal language often requires more than one tense or structure. Use the *imperfecto* for the background habit, the present perfect for relevant change, and relative clauses to identify people or situations precisely.
